positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description:
-Individually fully owned the “Design for Health” web application built in ASP.NET, C#, SQL Server, Umbraco, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with multiple environments in Azure, which was primarily used as a catalog for clients and public users
-Collaborated with marketing, auditing, and data engineering teams on a weekly basis to handled prioritization and ensure clients’ data were updated post audit to meet target requirements
-Independently managed data migrations from Snowflake to Azure SQL databases for ~30% (40/130) of client audits by end of Q2
-Updated the auditing process UX and data schema by replacing Qualtrics surveys with a Python and Streamlit integration
-Improved data analytics for auditing team and reduced manual inputs for clients

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
-Worked on a cross-functional team to build a new web app to handle contract creation and management
-Integrated with DocuSign API, allowing users to electronically sign documents and request signatures
-Transitioned UI from Vue to Blazor WASM to build custom widgets for a more interactive UI and increase development efficiency
-Created and maintained a microservice architecture using gRPC API endpoints and unit tests with ASP.NET Core and xUnit

positions.title: Associate Software Development Engineer
positions.description:
-Worked on an agile team to build a new web app for Colorado Community College System to consolidate their existing five web applications
-Integrated with SendGrid to trigger emails during workflow steps to improve cross-department communication
-Created and maintained REST API endpoints and integration/ unit tests using C#, Entity Framework Core, LINQ, xUnit, and SQL Server
-Developed React components such as selectors and modals using TypeScript, Redux, HTML, and CSS
-Contributed through project completion and remained as the final engineer to oversee post-production impact
-Founded and led the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion committee

positions.title: Voice Instructor
positions.description: Using my musical background, I've been working with people of all ages and skill levels. I always aim to build and maintain strong relationships with my students in order to best help them with their personal needs and goals, especially when it comes to building vocal technique and expanding repertoire.

positions.title: Student
positions.description:
GOOD APPLE - a web app for public school teachers to request financial contributions from community members to support students
•	Written in C# (ASP.NET core), using Entity Framework Core and LINQ queries
•	Used Bootstrap for frontend development
•	Implemented database using MySQL
•	Worked with one other developer to build out functionalities

ANIMAL SHELTER- a web app for users to add a pet to the shelter and/or adopt a pet; written in TypeScript 
•	Postman was used to make API calls
•	Angular was used to maintain single page functionalities
•	Express was used to allow MVC structure
•	Mongoose was used to set up models
•	MongoDB was used to set up the database

DOJO WALL- a web app for users to post messages, allowing other users to further comment on existing posts
•	Written in Python, using Django
•	SQLite was used to establish a database
•	Deployed through AWS using an EC2 instance

positions.title: Sustainability Intern
positions.description: As an intern with Seattle Good and Seattle Made, I conducted research on various markets, programs, and products in order to serve members of SM. In addition, I co-wrote a survey to collect data about business practices from SM members. I also updated the website to make information more readily available to potential SM members as well as the general public.

positions.title: Front Desk Staff
positions.description: During my time with the Peabody Institute Concert Office, I worked closely with my supervisors to maintain office organization in addition to helping any students and faculty who needed assistance. Other duties included answering phone calls and emails as well as processing all student recital programs.

testScores.name: Coding Dojo
testScores.description: Coding Dojo students take an exam at the end of each stack which consists of building a full web application in five hours. Building out the minimum requirements grants a student a red belt, achieving additional requirements grants a black belt. I received a black belt for each stack exam (Python, MEAN, and C#).
